correctness.rationale: The proof derives d=M/gcd(q,M) for the first rational iterate and the necessary-and-sufficient exact-order-two condition d>1, d|q+floor(qr/M). For every prime-power exponent it eliminates every smaller quotient using the exact floor range, constructs the least feasible quotient, verifies the least remainder (including p-coprimality for odd p), and handles denominator two separately. Exact Fraction computations independently exhausted 583945 smaller reduced numerators across 43 prime powers and validated 377 larger cases; these checks supplement rather than replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Carvalho explicitly poses the least-numerator problem and does not determine the all-prime-power order-two minima. The older Azevedo--Carvalho--Machiavelo map differs, and the origin paper does not cover rational minima. Published finding searches for aliases, reduced-denominator formulation, parity in prime-power exponents and stronger coverage returned no covering claim. The M=2 datum is acknowledged as prior; unindexed equivalences remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Published-result search coverage is not exhaustive; an equivalent unindexed or unpublished statement may exist.
The known M=2 case is prior-covered; only the all-prime-power classification beyond this special case is new.
General order-class enumeration in the motivating source could facilitate an independent derivation but does not state the minima.

value.rationale: Carvalho’s Question 3.5 isolates the natural least entrance numerator. The theorem completely computes it for the first nontrivial stopping time over all prime-power denominators, exhibits a sharp even/odd prime-power transition and a separate binary odd-exponent branch, and supplies exact globally minimal witnesses. This is a motivated infinite classification, not an arbitrary parameter table or routine reformulation of a count.
